cohort: The study included 46 women diagnosed with placenta previa and a matched control group of women with vaginal deliveries, drawn from 20,567 total deliveries evaluated over ten years at a single university hospital.
finding: Previous Cesarean Section was identified as the main risk factor for developing placenta previa, which in turn was associated with significantly longer maternal inpatient stays, increased hemorrhage, and worse neonatal outcomes including lower Apgar scores, lower birth weights, and higher NICU transfer rates due to prematurity.
mod_finding: Previous Cesarean Section was confirmed as the main risk factor for developing placenta previa in a subsequent pregnancy.
birth_weight: Mean 2404 grams (+- 671) for placenta previa group; Mean 3435 grams (+- 459) for control group.
